items.title: A closed subset nowhere dense in the generic fibre stays nowhere dense over a dense open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism over an irreducible base, if a closed subset is nowhere dense in the generic fibre then it is nowhere dense in every fibre over a nonempty open. The proof passes to the closure of the complement of the subset, spreads that closure to a neighbourhood using finite type and the irreducibility of the base, and then shows that the spread closure does not swallow any fibre over the open. Keeping the spread closure off the fibres is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 6532-6560.
